target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal setup needed a guided path that proves a usable receive transport before users rely on the channel, without OpenClaw creating or managing a Signal Docker container. Existing setup and status paths could also leave stale native/container transport fields ambiguous, miss account-specific API-mode behavior, or report a Signal daemon as generically working when the configured account was missing or receive was unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal plugin now owns a setup wizard path for two supported transports: local `signal-cli` and an existing Signal server managed by the operator. The same change tightens native/container/auto probing so setup and status can distinguish transport reachability from account/receive readiness, and it lets multi-account Signal configs use `channels.signal.apiMode` as a channel default with per-account overrides.

## User Impact

Users can run Signal setup, choose local `signal-cli` or an existing server URL, and have setup save config only after the selected transport is reachable for the intended account. Operators get clearer `openclaw channels status --probe` and health output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states. Existing/manual `bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api` deployments remain supported through `apiMode: "container"`; OpenClaw no longer offers an OpenClaw-managed Signal Docker setup path.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Existing-server setup prompts for a Signal account, probes the server with that account, and saves `httpUrl`, `autoStart: false`, and `apiMode: "auto"` after the probe succeeds.
- Native setup clears stale external/container endpoint fields for the intended account while preserving existing custom native endpoints and channel-level `channels.signal.apiMode` defaults.
- Container receive readiness is checked through `/v1/receive/{account}` when receive capability is required, and container account validation uses bounded `/v1/accounts` reads.
- Signal send, reaction, monitor, attachment, and probe paths resolve account-specific `apiMode` before falling back to the channel default.
- `openclaw channels status --probe` and health formatting expose Signal readiness states instead of reducing account-missing/receive-unavailable cases to a generic “works” signal.
- The setup copy now describes this as the same bounded setup pattern used by other connectors: native mode checks daemon/RPC reachability, while container mode also checks linked account and receive endpoint readiness.
- Screenshots are omitted because this PR changes terminal/setup wizard, gateway status, config, docs, and tests rather than browser UI; command output is the reviewer-checkable proof.

Automated checks on refreshed head `7ff67abdec4467bef91e5d5ebadda3b8a7f79f5c`:

- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check` passed.
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check` passed after regenerating the config docs baseline on the rebased tree.
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check` passed after regenerating the plugin SDK API baseline hash on the rebased tree.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/signal/src/setup-core.ts docs/channels/signal.md docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256 docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256 && git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- `node scripts/docs-list.js` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/setup-core.test.ts extensions/signal/setup-entry.test.ts` passed: 3 files, 100 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/setup-entry.test.ts extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/setup-core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/client-adapter.test.ts extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts extensions/signal/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/signal/src/install-signal-cli.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.pairs-uuid-only-senders-uuid-allowlist-entry.test.ts extensions/signal/src/send-reactions.test.ts extensions/signal/src/send.test.ts src/commands/channels.surfaces-signal-runtime-errors-channels-status-output.test.ts src/commands/health.test.ts` passed for the commands shard after one no-output retry and passed 10 Signal files before `extensions/signal/src/client.test.ts` timed out in an import hook during the large batch.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/client.test.ts` then passed alone: 1 file, 21 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts -- -t "lists the externalized provider and capability plugins with install metadata"` passed: 1 relevant catalog metadata test.
- The full `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts` file was not rerun after its unrelated HTTP-304 snapshot test timed out locally; the exact changed Signal catalog assertion passed by name.

Review proof:

- Phase 1 native review ran on `origin/main...HEAD` at `7ff67abdec4467bef91e5d5ebadda3b8a7f79f5c` and reported no discrete regressions in the changed Signal setup, probing, status, or per-account `apiMode` paths.
- Phase 2 cold review ran with a fresh isolated reviewer on the same local range and reported no blocking findings; it noted the only process caveat was that the local head had not yet been pushed at review time.
- Post-review fixes kept to accepted findings and mechanical refreshes only: three setup-core test clone calls use `structuredClone(...)`, configured-but-unlinked container accounts classify as `account_missing`, and generated config/plugin SDK baseline hashes were refreshed for the rebased head.

CI:

- Awaiting fresh PR checks for pushed head `7ff67abdec4467bef91e5d5ebadda3b8a7f79f5c`.
